question: What is the main focus of a community risk assessment?

options.A: Evaluating health hazards across an entire population
options.B: Treating emergency trauma cases in an accident unit
options.C: Checking the personal medical history of a local leader
options.D: Diagnosing rare diseases in individual hospital patients

explanation: Think of a community assessment like taking a bird's-eye view. Instead of looking at just one patient on a hospital bed, we look at collective health threats and environmental factors affecting everyone. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h1)

question: Why must a community health nurse look at both the environment and daily lifestyle of a population?

options.A: To trace the exact family tree of every community member
options.B: To understand the wide range of factors influencing public health
options.C: To fulfill government requirements for building new hospitals
options.D: To find out which residents have private health insurance

explanation: Spot on! People's health isn't just about germs; where they live, what they eat, and how they work all combine to shape their overall well-being. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h1)

question: What is the main goal of doing a community risk assessment?

options.A: Punishing communities that fail to follow sanitation laws
options.B: Reducing the total number of practicing nurses in a state
options.C: Preventing illness and health outbreaks before they occur
options.D: Generating revenue for private commercial pharmacies

explanation: Prevention is our superpower in public health! Finding risks early helps us stop sickness before it even starts. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h2)

question: How do risk assessment findings help local primary health care centers?

options.A: By allowing them to close down clinics with low patient numbers
options.B: By removing the need to keep paper medical records for patients
options.C: By automatically increasing the monthly salary of the clinic staff
options.D: By guiding them to direct scarce medical supplies where most needed

explanation: Resources are usually limited in our clinics. Clear data helps community nurses send drugs and mosquito nets precisely where the greatest need is. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h2)

question: Which of these is a classic example of an environmental community risk?

options.A: A sudden outbreak of a viral infection
options.B: A high rate of unemployment among youths

explanation: Bad water is a physical hazard right in the environment. It directly threatens everyone sharing that water source! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h3)

question: Why is an outbreak of cholera classified as a biological risk?

options.A: It is caused by living infectious agents spreading through a population
options.B: It only happens because of poor political leadership in the area
options.C: It arises purely from toxic factory smoke polluting the air
options.D: It is a social custom passed down from older generations

explanation: You got it! 'Biological' means living organisms—in this case, bacteria like Vibrio cholerae spreading through water or food. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h3)

question: What exactly is a windshield survey in community health?

options.A: Interviewing automobile drivers about local road accidents
options.B: Inspecting vehicles used for transporting emergency patients
options.C: Observing community conditions firsthand while moving through the area
options.D: Testing the window glass quality of local health clinics

explanation: Imagine driving or walking slowly through a neighborhood, looking at housing, open drainage, and market areas with your own eyes. That's a windshield survey! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h4)

question: Clinic records show few malaria cases, but local medicine vendors report selling lots of malaria drugs daily. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Report the clinic staff to the ministry for failing to do their jobs
options.B: Use community-based data collection like household surveys to find the real disease burden
options.C: Assume the medicine vendors are lying and close down their shops
options.D: Conclude that malaria has been completely eradicated in that area

explanation: Not everyone goes to the government clinic first; many buy drugs across the counter. To find the true picture, nurses must look beyond clinic logbooks and talk to the community directly. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h4)

question: In public health, what do we mean by 'vulnerable populations'?

options.A: Government officials responsible for funding local health clinics
options.B: Individuals who refuse to take prescribed hospital medications
options.C: Groups with a higher risk of poor health due to disadvantages
options.D: Wealthy citizens who travel abroad for routine medical checkups

explanation: Vulnerable groups—like pregnant mothers, infants, or the very poor—face extra hurdles that make it easier for them to fall sick. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h5)

question: Why must a community health nurse pay special attention to vulnerable groups during an assessment?

options.A: They often lack the voice or resources to access care on their own
options.B: They pay higher taxes to support the local primary health center
options.C: They make up the majority of the staff working in the hospitals
options.D: They are the only people in the community who ever get sick

explanation: Because these groups often suffer quietly without demanding services, it's our duty as nurses to actively find them and be their advocates. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h5)

question: What is the main reason health risks must be prioritized after an assessment?

options.A: Resources and funds are always limited
options.B: The government bans solving more than one problem
options.C: Nurses are not allowed to address environmental problems
options.D: Communities never suffer from more than two health issues

explanation: We would love to fix every single problem at once, but money and time are always limited. Prioritizing helps us tackle the most urgent issues first. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h6)

question: Why is it helpful to involve community members when prioritizing health problems?

options.A: It guarantees that no one will ever fall sick in the community again
options.B: It prevents the government from spending any money on the project
options.C: It removes the need for the nurse to write a formal health report
options.D: It ensures the chosen priority matches what the people care about most

explanation: When the community helps choose what to fix first, they feel respected and are much more willing to support the health project. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h6)

question: Who is considered a 'stakeholder' in community health engagement?

options.A: Patient relatives who refuse to pay hospital admission bills
options.B: Anyone with an interest or role in the community's health
options.C: Only the medical doctors working in the federal teaching hospital
options.D: Foreign donors who live outside the African continent

explanation: Stakeholders include local chiefs, youth leaders, market women, and residents—anyone who cares about and is affected by the community's health. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h7)

question: What is the main benefit of true community participation in health projects?

options.A: Nurses no longer need to visit the community for checkups
options.B: Residents take ownership of the project and ensure its long-term success
options.C: The cost of buying medical equipment drops to zero
options.D: The community becomes entirely independent of any government help

explanation: When the people feel the project belongs to them, they will protect and sustain it long after the nurses pack up and leave. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of a community health nursing care plan?

options.A: To replace all medical textbooks used in nursing schools
options.B: To punish community members who break environmental laws
options.C: To guide practical nursing actions and measure health outcomes
options.D: To serve as a decoration for the office wall of the clinic head

explanation: A care plan is your step-by-step roadmap. It tells you what actions to take, who is responsible, and how to check if things are getting better. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h8)

question: How does a risk assessment connect directly to a nursing care plan?

options.A: Nursing plans focus purely on hospital ward routines rather than community issues
options.B: Assessment findings identify the exact problems that the nursing plan aims to solve
options.C: Assessment data is only used for statistical research and never for nursing actions
options.D: Nursing plans are written first before any assessment is ever carried out

explanation: You assess first to discover the gaps (like dirty water or low immunization), and then you build your care plan to solve those exact problems! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h8)
